answers.84797: An exothermic reaction is one in which heat is released along with the products, for example CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + heat, or the burning of natural gas CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O + heat. An endothermic reaction is one in which heat is absorbed from the surroundings, for example the thermal decomposition of limestone CaCO3 + heat -> CaO + CO2, or photosynthesis, which absorbs energy from sunlight.
answers.84798: During respiration glucose combines with oxygen in the cells to form carbon dioxide and water, and energy is released: C6H12O6 + 6O2 -> 6CO2 + 6H2O + energy. answers.84799: In a combination reaction two or more substances join to form a single product, while in a decomposition reaction a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances. The two are therefore opposite in direction. For example, combination: CaO + CO2 -> CaCO3; decomposition: CaCO3 + heat -> CaO + CO2. Combination reactions are usually exothermic, whereas decomposition reactions generally need energy as heat, light or electricity.
answers.84800: In a displacement reaction a more reactive element takes the place of a less reactive one in a compound, and only one exchange happens: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu. In a double displacement reaction two compounds exchange their ions with each other, so two new compounds are formed: Na2SO4 + BaCl2 -> BaSO4 + 2NaCl. Double displacement reactions usually occur in solution and often give a precipitate.
answers.84801: Copper is more reactive than silver, so it displaces silver from silver nitrate solution: Cu(s) + 2AgNO3(aq) -> Cu(NO3)2(aq) + 2Ag(s). The silver settles out as a grey deposit and the solution turns blue because of the copper nitrate formed.
answers.84802: A precipitation reaction is one in which two solutions react to form an insoluble solid, called a precipitate, which separates from the solution. The second equation is simply the first one reversed, which is why decomposition is described as the opposite of combination.
